<analysis>
This session was a series of short test requests ("probes") in the sandbox repo C:\dev\strategos-sandbox. The user seems to be testing hooks and plugins (a "Strategos" hook and a "plain-talk" plugin). Going through it in order:

1. The user asked me to run `echo strategos-probe > probe.txt`, reply "done", and quote word for word any hook note containing STRATEGOS. I ran it and it printed nothing. A PostToolUse hook added the note "STRATEGOS-NOTE-7731". I replied done and quoted that note.
2. The user gave three lines: run the command; if it is denied, just say denied and stop; do nothing else. The Bash call was blocked with the error "Denied by the Strategos spike (S2 deny test)". I replied "Denied."
3. The user asked me to run the command, then say "ok". It worked and the same hook note came back. I replied "ok".
4. The plain-talk plugin sent a message, in the user's place, saying there was no evidence the command ran. Without running any tools, I rewrote the reply: ok, plus a note that the command ran with no output, and the Done / Not done / Your next step parts.
5. The user asked for the command again, then "ok2". It worked, and I replied ok2 with an explanation and the three parts.
6. The same again with "ok3". It worked, and I replied the same way.
7. The user asked me to use AskUserQuestion for a favourite colour (Red, Green, Blue) and reply with only the chosen colour. They answered Green, and I replied "Green".
8. The plain-talk plugin wrongly claimed I had not used AskUserQuestion. I replied "Green" plus a note that I did ask and they picked Green.
9. The user asked me to use AskUserQuestion for a favourite animal (Cat, Dog) and reply with only the chosen animal. They answered Dog, and I replied "Dog".
10. The plain-talk plugin made the same wrong claim. I replied "Dog" plus a note that I did ask and they picked Dog.
11. Now: the compact request ("AAA one/compact").

No code was changed apart from probe.txt. There were no security rules beyond the instruction to stop if denied.
</analysis>
